'''Eleanor Krawitz Kolchin''' (1927 - January 25, 2019) was an American mathematician, computer programmer, author, and teacher.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2021-07-22|title=The Watson Scientific Laboratory|url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/computinghistory/krawitz/index.html|access-date=2021-09-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210722041426/http://www.columbia.edu/cu/computinghistory/krawitz/index.html|archive-date=2021-07-22}}</ref> She worked at [[Watson Scientific Computing Laboratory]] at [[Columbia University]] to calculate the orbit of planets, phases of the moon, and trajectories of asteroids using [[IBM]] [[tabulating machine]]s.<ref name=":0" /> Her calculations were used in the [[Apollo program]].<ref name=":1" />

== Education ==
Eleanor attended [[Samuel J. Tilden High School]]<ref name=":0" /> where she took an interest in [[Euclidean geometry]] and graduated in 1943. She earned her B.A. in mathematics at [[Brooklyn College]] in January 1947. While there, she served as treasurer for [[Pi Mu Epsilon]], the national mathematics honor society.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Coast|first=Josh|date=2021-05-20|title=2014 NCWIT Summit - Eleanor Kolchin Pioneer Award Celebration {{!}} National Center for Women & Information Technology|url=https://ncwit.org/video/2014-ncwit-summit-eleanor-kolchin-pioneer-award-celebration/|access-date=2021-09-21|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Boch|first=Alone|date=June 23, 2021|title=Jewish Women in Computer Science|url=https://jwa.org/encyclopedia/article/jewish-women-in-computer-science|url-status=live|access-date=2021-09-23|website=Jewish Women's Archive|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210815024608/https://jwa.org/encyclopedia/article/jewish-women-in-computer-science |archive-date=2021-08-15 }}</ref> After graduating, she applied and was accepted to Columbia University, where she took classes towards her master's degree in mathematics.<ref name=":2" />

== Professional work ==
After high school, Eleanor took a job as a substitute teacher at the high school level at [[Midwood High School]] and later at her alma mater, Tilden High.<ref name=":0" />

In 1947, Kolchin was hired to work at IBM’s Thomas J. Watson Computing Laboratory at Columbia University.<ref name=":2" /> She was hired along with one woman and three men to take on a project at the Watson Laboratory operating tabulating machines for astrophysics. She simultaneously pursued a master's degree in Mathematics at Columbia while working in the laboratory.<ref name=":2" />

Kolchin was tabulating supervisor in the laboratory and taught in Columbia's astronomy department.<ref name=":2" />

She was the first woman to contribute to ''Columbia Engineering Quarterly.''<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bosker|first=Bianca|date=2013-02-01|title=This Is The Face Of A 'Computer' From 1946|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/watson-scientific-computing-lab_n_2592670|url-status=live|access-date=2021-09-24|website=HuffPost|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706154303/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/watson-scientific-computing-lab_n_2592670 |archive-date=2019-07-06 }}</ref>

In 1949, she published an article describing the Watson Lab’s work. It has since been translated into over 20 languages.<ref name=":2" />

* [[iarchive:bitsavers ibmproceedmputationSeminarSep50 8283585/page/n63/mode/2up|Krawitz, Eleanor, "Matrix by Vector Multiplication on the IBM Type 602-A Calculating Punch", ''Proceedings, Industrial Computation Seminar'', IBM, New York (Sep 1950), pp.66-70.]]

Weber, and Eleanor Krawitz, "The Use of Calculated and Observed Energies in the Computation of Oscillator Strengths and the f-Sum Rule", ''Astrophysical Journal'', Vol.113 No.3 (May 1951), pp.690-696.]
* [https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.96.319 Green, Louis C., Marjorie M. Mulder, Paul C. Milner, Margaret N. Lewis, John W. Woll, Jr., Eleanor K. Kolchin, and David Mace, "Analysis of the Three Parameter Wave Function of Hylleraas for the He i Ground State in Terms of Central Field Wave Functions", ''Physical Review 96'', 319, 15 October 1954.]

Baldwin, and Robert J. Wisner, "Effect on the Energy of Increased Flexibility in the Separable Factor of Hylleraas-Type Atomic Wave Functions from H− to O VII", ''Physical Review 112'', 1187, 15 November 1958.]
* Green, Louis C.; Matsushima, Satoshi; Kolchin, Eleanor K., "Tables of the Continuum Wave Functions for Hydrogen", ''Astrophysical Journal Supplement'', vol. 3, November 1958, p.&nbsp;459.

* Green, Louis C., Eleanor K. Kolchin, "Equi-density surfaces in synchronously rotating close binaries built on polytropic model ν=3", ''Astrophysics and Space Science'', Issue 2, April 1973, pp.&nbsp;285–288.

== Recognition ==
In 2014, she was presented The National Center for Women & Information Technology's Pioneer Award.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Coast|first=Josh|date=2021-05-20|title=2014 NCWIT Summit - Eleanor Kolchin Pioneer Award Celebration {{!}} National Center for Women & Information Technology|url=https://ncwit.org/video/2014-ncwit-summit-eleanor-kolchin-pioneer-award-celebration/|access-date=2021-09-24|language=en-US}}</ref>
